UNSAFE USE: after pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len) potentially reallocates the head, the stale pre-pull pointer ph is dereferenced for both read (ph->sb_type) and write (ph->sb_len -= 2) — a state transition through freed slab memory. CONSEQUENCE: slab use-after-free read/write on the RX path reachable from an unauthenticated/untrusted peer packet; KASAN-detectable UAF, potential info leak or memory corruption. TRANSFERABLE INVARIANT: any code that captures a pointer into a buffer that a subsequent call may realloc/free (skb head linearization being the canonical case) and dereferences it afterward without refetching is the same bug class, independent of protocol.
